qe: When Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South India in January 1915, he decided to travel for a year to understand public conditions. What political stance did he initially adopt regarding current agitations?
qh: जब महात्मा गांधी जनवरी 1915 में दक्षिण अफ्रीका से भारत लौटे, तो उन्होंने जनता की स्थिति को समझने के लिए एक वर्ष तक यात्रा करने का निर्णय लिया। उन्होंने वर्तमान आंदोलनों के संबंध में शुरू में क्या राजनीतिक रुख अपनाया?
o: He decided not to take any position on any political matter and was not in favor of the popular Home Rule agitation during the war
He immediately accepted the dynamic presidential chair of the All India Home Rule League
He launched an immediate pan-India mass strike against British military recruitment channels
He integrated his platform completely with the aristocratic landlords of the British Indian Association
e: Detailed Explanation: Upon his return in January 1915, Gandhi spent a year touring the country without taking political positions. He recognized the limits of Moderate politics and did not support the Home Rule agitation, believing it was inappropriate to agitate while Britain was engaged in the First World War.

qe: The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 marks Mahatma Gandhi's first battle of civil disobedience in India. Who was the local man who requested him to investigate the grievances of indigo cultivators?
qh: 1917 का चंपारण सत्याग्रह भारत में महात्मा गांधी के सविनय अवज्ञा के पहले संघर्ष को चिह्नित करता है। वह स्थानीय व्यक्ति कौन था जिसने उनसे नील उत्पादकों की शिकायतों की जांच करने का अनुरोध किया था?
o: Rajkumar Shukla
Brajkishore Prasad
Anugrah Narayan Sinha
Mazhar-ul-Haq
e: Detailed Explanation: Rajkumar Shukla, a local cultivator from Champaran, Bihar, traveled to meet Gandhi and persistently requested him to visit Champaran to look into the extreme exploitation of the peasants by European indigo planters.

qe: Under the exploitative 'tinkathia system' enforced by European planters in Champaran, what exact proportion of their total land were peasants legally forced to cultivate with indigo?
qh: चंपारण में यूरोपीय बागान मालिकों द्वारा लागू की गई शोषक 'तीनकठिया प्रणाली' (tinkathia system) के तहत, किसानों को अपनी कुल भूमि के किस सटीक अनुपात में नील की खेती करने के लिए कानूनी रूप से मजबूर किया गया था?
o: 3/20 part of the total land
1/3 part of the total land
5/20 part of the total land
Half of the total land area
e: Detailed Explanation: The tinkathia system was a colonial land obligation in Bihar where European planters forced peasants to cultivate indigo on 3 out of every 20 parts (3 katthis out of 1 bigha) of their total land holding.

qe: Toward the close of the 19th century, European indigo planters in Champaran faced a severe structural market shift that threatened their profit margins. What triggered this shift?
qh: 19वीं शताब्दी के अंत में, चंपारण में यूरोपीय नील बागान मालिकों को एक गंभीर संरचनात्मक बाजार परिवर्तन का सामना करना पड़ा जिसने उनके लाभ मार्जिन को खतरे में डाल दिया। इस बदलाव का क्या कारण था?
o: The invention and market replacement of natural indigo by German synthetic dyes
A complete legal ban on international maritime trade routes passed by the Crown
The sudden physical degradation of the soil fertility matrix across North Bihar plains
The compulsory implementation of the Sarda Act guidelines raising labor age limits
e: Detailed Explanation: When German synthetic dyes replaced natural indigo in the international market, natural indigo became unremunerative. To compensate for their losses before peasants could shift to other crops, European planters began demanding exorbitant rents and illegal dues.

qe: When Mahatma Gandhi arrived in Champaran to investigate peasant grievances, the colonial authorities ordered him to leave immediately. How did Gandhi react, establishing a historic precedent?
qh: जब महात्मा गांधी किसानों की शिकायतों की जांच करने के लिए चंपारण पहुंचे, तो औपनिवेशिक अधिकारियों ने उन्हें तुरंत क्षेत्र छोड़ने का आदेश दिया। गांधी ने कैसी प्रतिक्रिया दी, जिससे एक ऐतिहासिक मिसाल कायम हुई?
o: He defied the official order and preferred to face punishment, initiating civil disobedience
He retreated immediately to Calcutta to file a civil lawsuit inside the High Court room
He agreed to pay a flat registration fee to the district magistrate to purchase peace
He called for an immediate armed guerrilla parameter conflict against the police forces
e: Detailed Explanation: Gandhi's refusal to leave Champaran was the first active implementation of civil disobedience in India. By peacefully defying an unjust administrative order and declaring his readiness to face imprisonment, he forced the authorities to retreat and permit an inquiry.

qe: As a compromise settlement with the European planters during the Champaran inquiry committee proceedings, what percentage of the illegally extracted dues did Gandhi agree should be refunded to the peasants?
qh: चंपारण जांच समिति की कार्यवाही के दौरान यूरोपीय बागान मालिकों के साथ एक समझौते के तहत, गांधी अवैध रूप से वसूले गए बकाए का कितना प्रतिशत किसानों को वापस करने पर सहमत हुए?
o: 25 per cent
50 per cent
100 per cent
10 per cent
e: Detailed Explanation: To maintain the moral high ground and secure the abolition of the tinkathia system, Gandhi agreed to a compromise where planters would refund only 25 per cent of the illegally extracted money. This broke the planters' prestige, and they left the region within a decade.

qe: Which of the following sets of prominent regional leaders was actively associated with Mahatma Gandhi during the dynamic implementation of the Champaran Satyagraha in Bihar?
qh: बिहार में चंपारण सत्याग्रह के गतिशील कार्यान्वयन के दौरान निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा प्रमुख क्षेत्रीय नेताओं का समूह महात्मा गांधी के साथ सक्रिय रूप से जुड़ा हुआ था?
o: Rajendra Prasad, Mazhar-ul-Haq, Mahadeo Desai, Narhari Parekh, and J.B. Kripalani
Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Pherozshah Mehta, and Dinshaw Wacha exclusively
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, Mohanlal Pandya, and Ravi Shankar Vyas
Henry Vivian Derozio, Surendranath Banerjea, and Sisir Kumar Ghosh
e: Detailed Explanation: When Gandhi arrived in Bihar, he was joined by a brilliant cadre of educated young professionals and leaders, including Dr. Rajendra Prasad, Maulana Mazhar-ul-Haq, Mahadeo Desai, Narhari Parekh, and J.B. Kripalani, along with Brajkishore Prasad and Anugrah Narayan Sinha.

qe: In March 1918, Mahatma Gandhi intervened in a industrial dispute in Gujarat that led to his first hunger strike in India. What was the core issue of this conflict?
qh: मार्च 1918 में, महात्मा गांधी ने गुजरात में एक औद्योगिक विवाद में हस्तक्षेप किया, जिसके कारण भारत में उनकी पहली भूख हड़ताल हुई। इस संघर्ष का मुख्य मुद्दा क्या था?
o: The discontinuation of the plague bonus by the cotton mill owners of Ahmedabad
The forced extraction of land revenue during a severe drought in the Kheda district
The mandatory registration of all workers under the Anarchical Crimes Act regulation
The dynamic fluctuation of international raw jute prices entering the Calcutta port
e: Detailed Explanation: The Ahmedabad Mill Strike of 1918 was centered on a dispute between cotton mill owners and workers over the withdrawal of the 'plague bonus'. Workers demanded a wage hike to cope with severe wartime inflation, while owners refused.

qe: During the Ahmedabad industrial dispute, the workers faced arbitrary dismissals. Which social worker, who was also the sister of the Mill Owners' Association president, approached Gandhi to intervene?
qh: अहमदाबाद औद्योगिक विवाद के दौरान श्रमिकों को मनमाने ढंग से बर्खास्तगी का सामना करना पड़ा। मिल मालिक संघ के अध्यक्ष की बहन और सामाजिक कार्यकर्ता ने गांधी से हस्तक्षेप करने के लिए संपर्क किया था?
o: Anusuya Sarabhai
Sarada Devi
Sarojini Naidu
Kamladevi Chattopadhyaya
e: Detailed Explanation: Anusuya Sarabhai, a dedicated social worker and sister of the mill owners' association president Ambalal Sarabhai, championed the workers' cause and urged Gandhi to intervene to resolve the industrial deadlock.

qe: What precise percentage increase in wages did Mahatma Gandhi advise the striking Ahmedabad textile workers to demand, modifying their initial demand of 50 percent?
qh: महात्मा गांधी ने हड़ताली अहमदाबाद कपड़ा श्रमिकों को उनकी प्रारंभिक 50 प्रतिशत की मांग में संशोधन करते हुए मजदूरी में कितने सटीक प्रतिशत वृद्धि की मांग करने की सलाह दी थी?
o: 35 per cent increase
20 per cent increase
25 per cent increase
40 per cent increase
e: Detailed Explanation: Gandhi evaluated the economic realities of wartime inflation and advised the striking mill workers to lower their wage hike demand from 50 percent to a reasonable and justified 35 per cent increase.

qe: What strategic action did Mahatma Gandhi execute during the Ahmedabad mill dispute to strengthen the workers' sliding resolve and bring the employers to submit the matter to a tribunal?
qh: अहमदाबाद मिल विवाद के दौरान श्रमिकों के डगमगाते संकल्प को मजबूत करने और नियोक्ताओं को मामले को एक ट्रिब्यूनल को सौंपने के लिए मजबूर करने के लिए महात्मा गांधी ने कौन सा रणनीतिक कदम उठाया था?
o: He undertook a fast unto death, marking his first hunger strike in India
He filed a direct criminal injunction inside the central Imperial Legislative Council
He organized a paramilitary force armed with traditional clubs to occupy the mills
He ordered the workers to completely destroy all imported machine-loom assets
e: Detailed Explanation: To bolster the workers' determination during the prolonged strike, Gandhi undertook his first 'fast unto death' in India. This moral pressure forced the mill owners to compromise and agree to refer the dispute to an arbitration tribunal, which ultimately awarded the full 35 per cent wage hike.

qe: The Kheda Satyagraha of 1918 is recognized as Mahatma Gandhi's first non-cooperation movement in India. Under what structural condition were farmers legally entitled to full revenue remission according to the Revenue Code?
qh: 1918 का खेड़ा सत्याग्रह भारत में महात्मा गांधी के पहले असहयोग आंदोलन के रूप में मान्यता प्राप्त है। राजस्व संहिता (Revenue Code) के अनुसार किस संरचनात्मक स्थिति के तहत किसान कानूनी रूप से पूर्ण राजस्व छूट के हकदार थे?
o: If the agricultural crop yield was less than one-fourth of the normal produce due to failure
If the total continuous annual rainfall dropped below a negative baseline tracking metric
If the farmer surrendered half of his ancestral land holding to the Gujarat Sabha council
If the district was officially declared an active operational zone under the Rowlatt Act
e: Detailed Explanation: According to the colonial Revenue Code, if the crop yield fell below one-fourth of the normal average produce due to natural calamities like drought, the cultivators were legally entitled to a complete remission of land revenue.

qe: While Mahatma Gandhi acted as the spiritual head of the Kheda tax revolt, which frontline leader provided the active political and organizational leadership on the ground across the villages?
qh: जबकि महात्मा गांधी ने खेड़ा कर विद्रोह के आध्यात्मिक प्रमुख के रूप में कार्य किया, किस अग्रिम पंक्ति के नेता ने गांवों में सक्रिय राजनीतिक और संगठनात्मक नेतृत्व प्रदान किया?
o: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
Mohanlal Pandya
Ravi Shankar Vyas
Narahari Parikh
e: Detailed Explanation: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, alongside devoted young Gandhians like Mohanlal Pandya and Ravi Shankar Vyas, traveled through the villages of Kheda to organize the peasants, enforce strict non-violent discipline, and maintain solidarity against the seizure of properties.

qe: The Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act, which was passed by the Imperial Legislative Council in March 1919 to arm the state with extraordinary powers, is popularly known as the:
qh: औपनिवेशिक राज्य को असाधारण शक्तियों से लैस करने के लिए मार्च 1919 में इंपीरियल लेजिस्लेटिव काउंसिल द्वारा पारित अराजक और क्रांतिकारी अपराध अधिनियम (Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act) को लोकप्रिय रूप से किस नाम से जाना जाता है?
o: Rowlatt Act
Defence of India Regulations Act
Seditious Meetings Act
Criminal Law Amendment Act
e: Detailed Explanation: Officially titled the Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919, this repressive piece of legislation was popularly named the Rowlatt Act, after the commission's head, Sir Sidney Rowlatt.

qe: What drastic constitutional action did elected Indian members of the Imperial Legislative Council—including Jinnah, Malaviya, and Mazhar-ul-Haq—take to protest the passage of the Rowlatt Act?
qh: इंपीरियल लेजिस्लेटिव काउंसिल के निर्वाचित भारतीय सदस्यों - जिनमें जिन्ना, मालवीय और मज़ार-उल-हक शामिल थे - ने रौलट एक्ट के पारित होने के विरोध में कौन सा कड़ा संवैधानिक कदम उठाया?
o: They resigned from their legislative seats in protest
They filed a joint civil lawsuit before the High Court judges panel directly
They launched an immediate fast unto death inside the central council chamber
They ordered the complete physical blockade of all provincial revenue collectorates
e: Detailed Explanation: Although every elected Indian member voted against the Rowlatt Bill, they were in a minority and were outvoted by official nominees. In a sharp constitutional protest against this autocratic override, prominent leaders like Mohammed Ali Jinnah, Madan Mohan Malaviya, and Mazhar-ul-Haq resigned from the Council.

qe: The repressive provisions of the Rowlatt Act of 1919 stripped Indian citizens of basic civil liberties. Which extraordinary judicial parameter did it enforce against political suspects?
qh: 1919 के रौलट एक्ट के दमनकारी प्रावधानों ने भारतीय नागरिकों से बुनियादी नागरिक स्वतंत्रताएं छीन लीं। इसने राजनीतिक संदिग्धों के खिलाफ कौन सा असाधारण न्यायिक नियम लागू किया?
o: Arrest without warrant on mere suspicion of treason and trial in secrecy without a jury or right to appeal
The compulsory legal representation of all suspects by European high court barristers
An absolute requirement that all judicial decisions must be validated by local village panchayats
Exemption of all native vernacular newspaper printers from registration security deposits
e: Detailed Explanation: The Rowlatt Act authorized the state to arrest Indians without warrants on mere suspicion of treason and try them in secret tribunals without juries. Suspects were denied legal counsel, and the law barred any appeal above the panel of three High Court judges, effectively suspending habeas corpus.

qe: Mahatma Gandhi organized a specialized 'Satyagraha Sabha' to launch his first national-level mass strike against the Rowlatt Act. What date was initially chosen to observe the nationwide hartal?
qh: महात्मा गांधी ने रौलट एक्ट के खिलाफ अपना पहला राष्ट्रीय स्तर का सामूहिक हड़ताल शुरू करने के लिए एक विशेष 'सत्याग्रह सभा' का गठन किया। देशव्यापी हड़ताल (hartal) मनाने के लिए शुरू में कौन सी तारीख चुनी गई थी?
o: April 6, 1919
April 13, 1919
April 10, 1919
March 15, 1919
e: Detailed Explanation: Gandhi called for a nationwide hartal accompanied by fasting, prayer, and civil disobedience against the 'Black Act'. The mass protest was officially scheduled to be launched on April 6, 1919.

qe: The anti-British upsurge against the Rowlatt Act in April 1919 became exceptionally volatile in Punjab. Who was the Lieutenant Governor of Punjab who deployed harsh wartime repression and military force to crush the demonstrators?
qh: अप्रैल 1919 में रौलट एक्ट के खिलाफ ब्रिटिश विरोधी आंदोलन पंजाब में अत्यधिक उग्र हो गया था। पंजाब का लेफ्टिनेंट गवर्नर कौन था जिसने प्रदर्शनकारियों को कुचलने के लिए सख्त युद्धकालीन दमन और सैन्य बल का इस्तेमाल किया था?
o: Sir Michael O'Dwyer
Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer
Sir Sidney Rowlatt
Lord William Hunter
e: Detailed Explanation: Sir Michael O'Dwyer was the iron-fisted Lieutenant Governor of Punjab during the 1919 unrest. He implemented severe repressive measures, including the arrest of popular leaders, and even used aircraft strafing against protesters.

qe: The unprovoked arrest of which two prominent nationalist leaders on April 9, 1919, by British officials directly triggered intense public resentment and subsequent riots in Amritsar?
qh: ब्रिटिश अधिकारियों द्वारा 9 अप्रैल, 1919 को किन दो प्रमुख राष्ट्रवादी नेताओं की अकारण गिरफ्तारी ने सीधे तौर पर अमृतसर में तीव्र जन असंतोष और उसके बाद के दंगों को जन्म दिया?
o: Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr. Satyapal
Lala Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh
Mazhar-ul-Haq and Rajendra Prasad
Subramania Siva and Chidambaram Pillai
e: Detailed Explanation: The peaceful atmosphere in Amritsar turned volatile after the colonial administration abruptly arrested two popular local leaders, Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr. Satyapal, on April 9 and deported them to an undisclosed location.

qe: Following early riots in Amritsar, which senior British military officer was armed with the immediate responsibility to enforce martial law and restore administrative order in the city?
qh: अमृतसर में शुरुआती दंगों के बाद, किस वरिष्ठ ब्रिटिश सैन्य अधिकारी को शहर में मार्शल लॉ लागू करने और प्रशासनिक व्यवस्था बहाल करने की तत्काल जिम्मेदारी सौंपी गई थी?
o: Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer
Sir Michael O'Dwyer
Lord William Hunter
Winston Churchill
e: Detailed Explanation: Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer was handed operational command of the troops sent to Amritsar. He imposed strict martial law restrictions, including a ban on public gatherings of more than three people.

qe: On April 13, 1919, thousands of people gathered in the enclosed Jallianwala Bagh on the festival day of Baisakhi. What specific political resolutions had been passed peacefully by the assembly right before the arrival of the troops?
qh: 13 अप्रैल, 1919 को बैसाखी के त्योहार के दिन हजारों लोग जलियांवाला बाग में एकत्र हुए थे। सैनिकों के आगमन से ठीक पहले सभा द्वारा कौन से विशिष्ट राजनीतिक प्रस्ताव शांतिपूर्वक पारित किए गए थे?
o: A resolution calling for the repeal of the Rowlatt Act and another condemning the police firing of April 10
A programmatic charter demanding the immediate establishment of the Swarajya Sabha council
A legal petition seeking the complete merger of the Supreme Court and High Court benches
An official proclamation declaring absolute armed non-cooperation against the British Crown
e: Detailed Explanation: The gathering in the Bagh was peaceful. Before General Dyer arrived with his troops, the assembly had passed two formal resolutions: one demanding the immediate repeal of the repressive Rowlatt Act, and another condemning the unprovoked police firings that took place on April 10.

qe: What precise mechanical deployment did Brigadier-General Dyer execute when he trapped the unarmed gathering inside Jallianwala Bagh on April 13, 1919?
qh: ब्रिगेडियर-जनरल डायर ने 13 अप्रैल, 1919 को जलियांवाला बाग के भीतर निहत्थी भीड़ को फंसाकर कौन सा कड़ा सैन्य कदम उठाया था?
o: His troops surrounded the gathering, blocked the only narrow exit point, and opened fire without issuing any warning to disperse
He deployed aircraft strafing directly over the central open arena to disperse the crowd instantly
He ordered a standard acid-base chemical titration gas to be released into the bulk solution area
He executed a formal verification check requiring every individual to register their thumb impressions
e: Detailed Explanation: General Dyer arrived with troops and armored cars. He blocked the sole narrow exit of the walled garden and ordered his men to open fire on the trapped, unarmed gathering of men, women, and children without giving any order or warning to disperse.

qe: According to official data metrics recorded from the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, exactly how many bullets were fired by British Indian troops into the fleeing crowd?
qh: जलियांवाला बाग हत्याकांड के दर्ज आधिकारिक आंकड़ों के अनुसार, ब्रिटिश भारतीय सैनिकों द्वारा भागती हुई भीड़ पर सटीक रूप से कितनी गोलियां चलाई गई थीं?
o: 1650 bullets
379 bullets
1100 bullets
1500 bullets
e: Detailed Explanation: Historical logs show that the troops continued firing for 10 to 15 minutes until their ammunition was nearly exhausted, firing exactly 1650 rounds of bullets into the crowd.

qe: In a profound symbolic gesture of national protest against the uncivilized brutalities perpetrated under martial law in Punjab, Rabindranath Tagore renounced which title?
qh: पंजाब में मार्शल लॉ के तहत किए गए अमानवीय अत्याचारों के खिलाफ राष्ट्रीय विरोध के एक गहरे प्रतीकात्मक कदम के रूप में, रवींद्रनाथ टैगोर ने किस उपाधि का त्याग कर दिया था?
o: Knighthood
Kaiser-i-Hind
Lokmanya
Mahatma
e: Detailed Explanation: Deeply shocked by the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and the subsequent public floggings, Rabindranath Tagore wrote a letter to the Viceroy renouncing his British Knighthood, stating that such badges of honor made their shame glaring in the context of humiliation.

qe: Mahatma Gandhi surrendered his 'Kaiser-i-Hind' gold medal after the Jallianwala Bagh tragedy. For what specific historical work had this medal been bestowed upon him by the British?
qh: जलियांवाला बाग त्रासदी के बाद महात्मा गांधी ने अपना 'कैसर-ए-हिंद' (Kaiser-i-Hind) स्वर्ण पदक वापस कर दिया था। अंग्रेजों द्वारा उन्हें यह पदक किस विशिष्ट ऐतिहासिक कार्य के लिए प्रदान किया गया था?
o: His humanitarian work during the Boer War in South Africa
His successful leadership of the Champaran peasant civil disobedience battle
Organizing the elite Simla Deputation front to petition Lord Minto
Compiling standard modern elegancies prose style grammar text items
e: Detailed Explanation: Gandhi had been awarded the Kaiser-i-Hind medal by the British government for his service in organizing an ambulance corps during the Boer War. He renounced it in 1819, declaring that cooperation with a 'satanic regime' was no longer morally possible.

qe: Which prominent revolutionary nationalist later assassinated Michael O'Dwyer, the former Lieutenant-Governor of Punjab, to avenge the brutal suppression of the 1919 protests?
qh: किस प्रमुख क्रांतिकारी राष्ट्रवादी ने 1919 के प्रदर्शनों के क्रूर दमन का बदला लेने के लिए पंजाब के पूर्व लेफ्टिनेंट-गवर्नर माइकल ओ'डायर की हत्या कर दी थी?
o: Udham Singh
Bhagat Singh
Sardar Ajit Singh
Mohanlal Pandya
e: Detailed Explanation: Udham Singh (who chose the symbolic name Ram Mohammad Singh Azad) traveled to London and assassinated Sir Michael O'Dwyer in 1940, holding him responsible for the structural atrocities and martial law brutalities inflicted on Punjab in 1919.

qe: The Government of India announced the formation of the 'Disorders Inquiry Committee' in October 1919 to investigate the massacres. This committee is widely known by which name?
qh: भारत सरकार ने हत्याकांडों की जांच के लिए अक्टूबर 1919 में 'डिसऑर्डर इनक्वायरी कमेटी' (Disorders Inquiry Committee) के गठन की घोषणा की। इस समिति को व्यापक रूप से किस नाम से जाना जाता है?
o: Hunter Committee
Rowlatt Commission
Simon Commission
Macaulay Law Commission
e: Detailed Explanation: The official investigation body was named the Disorders Inquiry Committee, but it became popularly known as the Hunter Committee, after its chairman, Lord William Hunter.

qe: To investigate the baseline truth, three distinguished Indian members were included on the Hunter Committee panel. Who were these members?
qh: बुनियादी सच्चाई की जांच करने के लिए, हंटर कमेटी के पैनल में तीन प्रतिष्ठित भारतीय सदस्यों को शामिल किया गया था। ये सदस्य कौन थे?
o: Sir Chimanlal Harilal Setalvad, Pandit Jagat Narayan, and Sardar Sahibzada Sultan Ahmad Khan
Mohammed Ali Jinnah, Madan Mohan Malaviya, and Mazhar-ul-Haq
Dr. Rajendra Prasad, Anugrah Narayan Sinha, and Brajkishore Prasad
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, Narahari Parikh, and Mohanlal Pandya
e: Detailed Explanation: The Hunter Committee included three prominent Indian legal experts: Sir Chimanlal Harilal Setalvad (Vice-Chancellor of Bombay University), Pandit Jagat Narayan (lawyer from the United Provinces), and Sardar Sahibzada Sultan Ahmad Khan (lawyer from Gwalior State).

qe: When examined before the Hunter Committee, General Dyer confidently justified his actions. What shocking logic did he offer for not tending to the wounded after the shooting?
qh: हंटर कमेटी के सामने जांच के दौरान जनरल डायर ने अपने कार्यों को सही ठहराया। शूटिंग के बाद घायलों की देखभाल न करने के संबंध में उन्होंने क्या चौंकाने वाला तर्क दिया था?
o: He explicitly stated that he did not consider it his job or duty to tend to the wounded
He claimed that all exit points were blocked by the Indian National Congress volunteers
He argued that there was an acute scarcity of non-ionic medical fluid solutions locally
He stated that the wounded refused to accept help unless provided by Indian officers
e: Detailed Explanation: General Dyer showed no remorse before the commission. He stated his intention was to strike terror across Punjab to reduce the moral stature of the rebels, and bluntly added that he did not provide any medical aid to the hundreds of wounded because he did not consider it his duty.

qe: The minority report submitted separately by the Indian members of the Hunter Committee condemned Dyer's actions using which precise operational classification?
qh: हंटर कमेटी के भारतीय सदस्यों द्वारा अलग से प्रस्तुत की गई अल्पसंख्यक रिपोर्ट (minority report) ने किस सटीक परिचालन वर्गीकरण का उपयोग करके डायर के कार्यों की निंदा की थी?
o: They declared his actions to be utterly 'inhuman and un-British', heavily damaging the image of British rule
They classified his military deployment as a fully justified application of the Defence of India Act
They certified the incident as a minor localized disturbance triggered by non-registered newspaper activate loops
They defined his parameters as a standard compliance technique aligned with Lord Macaulay’s charter
e: Detailed Explanation: The three Indian members signed a separate minority report that strongly condemned the massacre. They noted that the prohibitory orders were insufficiently publicized, the crowd was peaceful beforehand, and labeled Dyer's actions as entirely 'inhuman and un-British'.

qe: Before the Hunter Committee could even begin its official proceedings, the colonial government passed a protective piece of legislation known as the Indemnity Act. What was its popular critical nickname?
qh: हंटर कमेटी द्वारा अपनी आधिकारिक कार्यवाही शुरू करने से पहले ही, औपनिवेशिक सरकार ने एक सुरक्षात्मक कानून पारित किया जिसे इनडेम्निटी एक्ट (Indemnity Act) कहा गया। इसका लोकप्रिय आलोचनात्मक उपनाम क्या था?
o: The white washing bill
The gagging Act
The black Act
The sunless dawn regulation
e: Detailed Explanation: To shield its military and civil officers from legal accountability or future prosecution for atrocities committed during martial law, the government passed an Indemnity Act in advance. Motilal Nehru and other nationalist leaders severely criticized this protective law, labeling it 'the white washing bill'.

qe: Which prominent British statesman, serving as the Secretary of State for War at that time, reviewed the report and officially condemned the Amritsar massacre in the House of Commons as 'monstrous'?
qh: किस प्रमुख ब्रिटिश राजनेता ने, जो उस समय युद्ध के राज्य सचिव (Secretary of State for War) के रूप में कार्यरत थे, रिपोर्ट की समीक्षा की और हाउस ऑफ कॉमन्स में अमृतसर हत्याकांड की आधिकारिक तौर पर 'monstrous' (क्रूर) कहकर निंदा की?
o: Winston Churchill
Edwin Montagu
H.H. Asquith
Rudyard Kipling
e: Detailed Explanation: Winston Churchill, serving as the Secretary of State for War, reviewed the findings and delivered a speech in the House of Commons condemning the Amritsar incident as 'monstrous' and an un-British outrage. This directly led to the Army Council recalling Dyer and relieving him of command.

qe: The baseline orientation of the Indian national movement underwent a permanent structural transformation during the anti-Rowlatt agitations. What was this transformation?
qh: रौलट-विरोधी आंदोलनों के दौरान भारतीय राष्ट्रीय आंदोलन का बुनियादी रुख एक स्थायी संरचनात्मक परिवर्तन से गुजरा। यह परिवर्तन क्या था?
o: The orientation of the national movement turned to the masses permanently, involving peasants, artisans, and the urban poor
The movement restricted its focus exclusively to sending long written petitions to the British Parliament
The leadership parameter shifted entirely to favor the wealthy pro-British merchants based in London
The movement abandoned its political character to operate solely as a network of agricultural banks
e: Detailed Explanation: The Rowlatt Satyagraha was a watershed moment. It permanently shifted the focus of the national movement from urban elitist constitutional debates to the masses, bringing peasants, artisans, and the urban poor into active politics under Gandhi's leadership.

qe: The shocking incident where the clergy of the Golden Temple, led by Arur Singh, honored General Dyer by declaring him a 'Sikh' directly intensified the public demand for which historical reform movement?
qh: अरुर सिंह के नेतृत्व में स्वर्ण मंदिर के पादरियों द्वारा जनरल डायर को 'सिख' घोषित करके सम्मानित करने की चौंकाने वाली घटना ने किस ऐतिहासिक सुधार आंदोलन की मांग को सीधे तेज कर दिया?
o: The Gurudwara Reform movement (or Akali movement)
The Singh Sabha educational network expansion
The traditional Bhakti cult revival across Punjab
The Satyashodhak Samaj anti-clerical campaign
e: Detailed Explanation: Public anger erupted when the corrupt, government-backed priests of Sri Darbar Sahib (Golden Temple) honored General Dyer. This action alienated the Sikh masses and directly intensified the demand to reform the management of Sikh shrines, leading to the launch of the Gurudwara Reform or Akali Movement.

qe: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre is evaluated by prominent historians as a decisive moment in modern Indian history because:
qh: प्रमुख इतिहासकारों द्वारा जलियांवाला बाग हत्याकांड का मूल्यांकन आधुनिक भारतीय इतिहास में एक निर्णायक मोड़ के रूप में किया जाता है क्योंकि:
o: It was the decisive moment when the masses of Indians were permanently alienated from British rule
It successfully established a robust responsible parliamentary government across all provinces
It completely eliminated the economic drain caused by the remittance of civil service pensions
It forced the absolute legal separation of the provincial judicial courts from executive oversight
e: Detailed Explanation: As noted by historians like A.J.P. Taylor, the Jallianwala Bagh tragedy was the decisive moment that shattered any remaining faith in British justice. It completely alienated the Indian population from colonial rule, making future non-cooperation inevitable.

qe: A tracking vehicle leaves base O and moves dynamically 40 km North, and then changes its course to drive 42 km East to reach checkpoint B. Find the straight-line distance from O to B.
qh: एक वाहन बेस O से निकलता है और 40 किमी उत्तर की ओर चलता है, और फिर दिशा बदलकर पूर्व की ओर 42 किमी जाकर चेकपॉइंट B पर पहुँचता है। O से B की सीधी रेखा की दूरी ज्ञात कीजिए।
o: 58 km
82 km
60 km
56 km
e:
Detailed Explanation: This spatial movement forms a right-angled triangle with perpendicular legs of 40 km and 42 km. The direct straight-line distance is the hypotenuse.
Applying the Pythagoras theorem: $\text{Distance} = \sqrt{40^2 + 42^2} = \sqrt{1600 + 1764} = \sqrt{3364} = \mathbf{58\text{ km}}$.

qe: In a biological ecosystem study tracking energy metrics, if the Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) of an alluvial plain is 52,000 units and the measured Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is 32,000 units, calculate the energy spent during plant metabolic respiration (R).
qh: ऊर्जा मापदंडों का मानचित्रण करने वाले एक पारिस्थितिकी उत्पादकता सर्वेक्षण में, यदि सकल प्राथमिक उत्पादकता (GPP) 52,000 इकाइयाँ है और मापी गई शुद्ध प्राथमिक उत्पादकता (NPP) 32,000 इकाइयाँ है, तो पौधों के श्वसन (R) के दौरान खर्च की गई ऊर्जा की गणना करें।
o: 20,000 units
84,000 units
30,000 units
16,000 units
e:
Detailed Explanation: Utilizing the core ecological productivity balance formula: $NPP = GPP - R$, we rewrite it to isolate respiration losses: $R = GPP - NPP$.
Substituting the values: $R = 52,000 - 32,000 = \mathbf{20,000\text{ units}}$.

qe: The British newspaper 'Morning Post' launched a high-profile fund-raising campaign in England for General Dyer upon his recall. Who was a famous literary contributor to this controversial fund?
qh: ब्रिटिश समाचार पत्र 'मॉर्निंग पोस्ट' ने जनरल डायर की वापसी पर इंग्लैंड में उनके लिए एक हाई-प्रोफाइल फंड जुटाने का अभियान शुरू किया था। इस विवादास्पद फंड में एक प्रसिद्ध साहित्यिक योगदानकर्ता कौन था?
o: Rudyard Kipling
Winston Churchill
Edwin Montagu
Valentine Chirol
e: Detailed Explanation: Despite official condemnation, a large section of the British public and the House of Lords viewed Dyer as the 'Saviour of India'. The Morning Post newspaper raised a massive sum of 26,000 pounds for him, and the famous author Rudyard Kipling was among the prominent contributors.

qe: What structural role did the 'Satyagraha Sabha' serve within Mahatma Gandhi's organizational layout during the anti-Rowlatt Act campaign in early 1919?
qh: 1919 की शुरुआत में रौलट एक्ट विरोधी अभियान के दौरान महात्मा गांधी के संगठनात्मक ढांचे के भीतर 'सत्याग्रह सभा' ने क्या विशिष्ट भूमिका निभाई थी?
o: It functioned as the organizational base to rope in younger members of Home Rule Leagues and Pan-Islamists for coordinated mass protest actions
It operated as an alternative high court panel to legally try British civil servants for war crimes
It was designed strictly to raise corporate capital inputs to establish swadeshi cotton textile mills
It managed the direct allocation of central legislative seats among different provinces
e: Detailed Explanation: To launch an effective pan-India protest against the Rowlatt Act, Gandhi established the Satyagraha Sabha. This organizational body brought together the energized younger members of the Home Rule Leagues and Pan-Islamist activists, coordinating the nationwide hartal.

qe: The dynamic experience of the 1919 Punjab suppression and Jallianwala Bagh massacre directly influenced a localized resistance group named 'Bharat Naujawan Sabha'. Who was inspired by this legacy during his youth?
qh: 1919 के पंजाब दमन और जलियांवाला बाग हत्याकांड के गतिशील अनुभव ने 'भारत नौजवान सभा' नामक एक स्थानीय प्रतिरोध समूह को सीधे प्रभावित किया। अपने युवाओं के दौरान इस विरासत से कौन प्रेरित था?
o: Bhagat Singh
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
Udham Singh
Sardar Ajit Singh
e: Detailed Explanation: Bhagat Singh was just 11 years old during the 1919 massacre. The memory of Jallianwala Bagh became a core revolutionary symbol for his organization, the Bharat Naujawan Sabha, helping them overcome political apathy and build a militant resistance movement.

qe: During the Kheda Satyagraha of 1918, the colonial government remained adamant and threatened peasants with severe consequences if taxes were not paid. What primary retaliatory action did the state execute?
qh: 1918 के खेड़ा सत्याग्रह के दौरान, औपनिवेशिक सरकार अड़ी रही और करों का भुगतान न करने पर किसानों को गंभीर परिणाम भुगतने की धमकी दी। राज्य ने कौन सी प्राथमिक प्रतिशोधात्मक कार्रवाई की?
o: Seizing the peasants' personal property, land, and livelihood livestock
The immediate administrative deportation of all primary producers to London
The complete physical destruction of the newly opened Ahmedabad textile mills
Imposing a flat registration fee threshold on the members of the Gujarat Sabha
e: Detailed Explanation: When the peasants of Kheda refused to pay land revenue due to crop failure, the colonial state retaliated by deploying coercive revenue machinery to seize their personal property, confiscate their lands, and attach their cattle and livelihoods.

qe: How did the local population in Kheda and other parts of Gujarat maintain solidarity and structurally neutralize the government's attempts to auction off confiscated peasant lands?
qh: खेड़ा और गुजरात के अन्य हिस्सों में स्थानीय आबादी ने एकजुटता कैसे बनाए रखी और जब्त की गई किसान भूमि को नीलाम करने के सरकार के प्रयासों को संरचनात्मक रूप से कैसे विफल किया?
o: Any Indian who sought to buy the confiscated lands was completely socially ostracized
They filed a joint property lawsuit inside the newly constituted Federal Court room
They completely burned all land record registers inside the local munsiff courts
They used non-caloric artificial sweetening agents to corrupt the soil solutions of auctioned lands
e: Detailed Explanation: The Kheda tax revolt was marked by remarkable non-violent discipline. To defend their peers, the community implemented a total social boycott against anyone who attempted to purchase the confiscated lands at government auctions, forcing the state to compromise.

qe: What final terms of agreement did the colonial government compromise upon to conclude the Kheda Satyagraha following the intense non-violent resistance of the peasantry?
qh: किसानों के तीव्र अहिंसक प्रतिरोध के बाद खेड़ा सत्याग्रह को समाप्त करने के लिए औपनिवेशिक सरकार ने समझौते के किन अंतिम शर्तों को स्वीकार किया?
o: It agreed to suspend the revenue tax for the year in question and the next, reduce the increase in rate, and return all confiscated property
It mandated that 100% of all future land revenues must be managed directly by the Indian National Congress
It completely transformed the Kheda district into an autonomous province free from the Viceroy's executive oversight
It forced the European mill owners to provide an absolute 50 percent wage hike to all laborers permanently
e: Detailed Explanation: Faced with a united peasant resistance, the government issued secret orders to suspend revenue collection for the current and subsequent years, reduced the tax rate increase, and returned all attached properties to their original owners.

qe: The 'Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association', which later developed into a powerful institutional front for industrial labor welfare, was established in 1920 by which leader?
qh: अहमदाबाद टेक्सटाइल लेबर एसोसिएशन (Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association), जो बाद में औद्योगिक श्रम कल्याण के लिए एक शक्तिशाली संस्थागत मोर्चा बना, की स्थापना 1920 में किस नेता द्वारा की गई थी?
o: Anusuya Sarabhai
Mahatma Gandhi
Ambalal Sarabhai
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
e: Detailed Explanation: Following her close collaboration with Gandhi during the 1918 mill strike, the social worker Anusuya Sarabhai (Anusuya Behn) went on to formally organize and found the Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association in 1920.

qe: Rethinking political tools, what did the three early localized campaigns—Champaran, Ahmedabad, and Kheda—demonstrate to the general public of India regarding Mahatma Gandhi’s leadership?
qh: राजनीतिक उपकरणों पर पुनर्विचार करते हुए, तीन शुरुआती स्थानीय अभियानों - चंपारण, अहमदाबाद और खेड़ा - ने महात्मा गांधी के नेतृत्व के संबंध में भारत की आम जनता को क्या प्रदर्शित किया?
o: They brilliantly demonstrated the practical efficacy and operational power of his technique of Satyagraha
They proved that national independence could be won solely through sending petitions to the British Parliament
They demonstrated that primary producers must remain completely aloof from any political organizations
They proved that the judicial high court benches could be easily manipulated using non-ionic liquid financial credits
e: Detailed Explanation: The triple victories in Champaran, Ahmedabad, and Kheda served as a historic laboratory for Gandhi's methods. They demonstrated to the country the practical power of Satyagraha (truth-force), establishing his position as a mass leader and earning him the respect of the youth.

qe: The Rowlatt Act of 1919 allowed a specialized judicial cell consisting of three high court judges to try political suspects in secrecy. What regressive evidence parameter was this panel authorized to accept?
qh: 1919 के रौलट एक्ट ने तीन उच्च न्यायालय के न्यायाधीशों वाले एक विशेष न्यायिक सेल को गुप्त रूप से राजनीतिक संदिग्धों पर मुकदमा चलाने की अनुमति दी थी। यह पैनल किस प्रतिगामी साक्ष्य नियम (evidence parameter) को स्वीकार करने के लिए अधिकृत था?
o: The panel could accept evidence not acceptable under the standard Indian Evidences Act
It required all evidence to be compiled exclusively in classical Sanskrit text scripts
The judges could only accept evidence that had been verified by a joint jury of local village panchayats
It barred the prosecution from presenting any testimonies given by British administrative officials
e: Detailed Explanation: To ensure convictions, the Rowlatt Act overrode regular judicial protections. The special three-judge panel was legally empowered to accept evidence that was strictly inadmissible under the standard Indian Evidence Act, eliminating fair trial parameters.

qe: What was the core underlying object of the colonial government when it forcefully passed the permanent Rowlatt Act framework in March 1919?
qh: मार्च 1919 में स्थायी रौलट एक्ट ढांचे को जबरन पारित करने के पीछे औपनिवेशिक सरकार का मूल उद्देश्य क्या था?
o: To replace the temporary, repressive provisions of the wartime Defence of India Act (1915) with a permanent law
To implement the financial decentralization recommendations outlined by the Royal Commission on Decentralization
To transfer the absolute supervisory control over central subjects directly to popular provincial ministries
To provide massive financial subsidies to support newly established swadeshi matching factories
e: Detailed Explanation: As the wartime Defence of India Act of 1915 was nearing expiration, the government sought a permanent mechanism to suppress the rising tide of nationalism. The Rowlatt Act was passed to permanently retain these restrictive powers, including constraints on free speech and assembly.

qe: The administrative scope of the Disorders Inquiry Committee (1919) was precisely defined at its inception. Which specific geographical regions was the Hunter Committee mandated to investigate?
qh: डिसऑर्डर्स इनक्वायरी कमेटी (1919) का प्रशासनिक दायरा इसके प्रारंभ में ही सटीक रूप से परिभाषित किया गया था। हंटर कमेटी को किन विशिष्ट भौगोलिक क्षेत्रों की जांच करने का आदेश दिया गया था?
o: The recent disturbances in Bombay, Delhi, and Punjab
The indigo plantation fields across Champaran, Bihar exclusively
The industrial strikes occurring within the jute mills of Bengal delta plains
The maritime ship-building ports of Surat, Malabar, and Masulipatnam
e: Detailed Explanation: The official warrant of appointment mandated the Hunter Committee to comprehensively investigate the causes of the recent civil disturbances that erupted across Bombay, Delhi, and Punjab, and evaluate the measures deployed by the state to handle them.

qe: The final report of the Hunter Committee, released in March 1920, reached several unanimous conclusions regarding the Jallianwala Bagh shooting. Which of the following reflects a conclusion of the committee?
qh: मार्च 1920 में जारी हंटर कमेटी की अंतिम रिपोर्ट में जलियांवाला बाग गोलीकांड के संबंध में कई सर्वसम्मत निष्कर्ष निकाले गए। निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा समिति के निष्कर्ष को दर्शाता है?
o: The length of firing showed a grave error, and Dyer's motive of producing a moral effect was to be condemned
There was an active, well-organized armed conspiracy to overthrow British rule in Punjab beforehand
Dyer acted fully within the standard constitutional bounds of his military executive authority
The proclamations banning public assemblies were perfectly and sufficiently publicized everywhere
e: Detailed Explanation: The official report concluded that while martial law was justified, General Dyer committed a grave error in continuing to fire for so long. It explicitly condemned his motive of producing a 'moral effect' on Punjab and concluded that he had overstepped the bounds of his authority.

qe: What final disciplinary or legal penalty was officially imposed on Brigadier-General Dyer by the British authorities back in England following the conclusion of the inquiries?
qh: जांच समाप्त होने के बाद इंग्लैंड में ब्रिटिश अधिकारियों द्वारा ब्रिगेडियर-जनरल डायर पर आधिकारिक रूप से कौन सा अंतिम अनुशासनात्मक या कानूनी दंड लगाया गया था?
o: He was found guilty of a mistaken notion of duty, relieved of his command in March 1920, and recalled to England on half pay and pension
He was sentenced to twenty years of rigorous transportation inside the Cellular Jail in the Andaman Islands
He was completely stripped of his military pension and faced a criminal trial before a high court jury in London
No action was taken, and he was promoted to the supreme office of the Chief of Defence Staff operational council
e: Detailed Explanation: General Dyer faced no criminal trial or imprisonment. The Cabinet, agreeing with Winston Churchill, found him guilty of a mistaken notion of duty and relieved him of his command in March 1920. He was recalled to England, where he retired on half pay and drew his standard army pension.
